facts.text: In early August the route held no snow; small leftover patches near the notch and under the summit can be melted for water, but still carry roughly 4 to 5 litres from the creek.
In the gully beneath the Anvil, the right-hand fork is the correct one; the left leads to the wrong side of the ridge.
60 m rope and rock shoes (July-September, for the roped upper pitches)
In August the Cascadian descent is long and loose; watch for the trail turn-off near 6,000 ft that leads out to the creek and trailhead, as missing it costs a lot of effort.
In July, wandering off line below the notch can force extra roped pitches; check the topo photos before leaving camp.
Warm July nights allow a comfortable open bivouac at the notch or on the summit without a tent.

season.evidence: Logged Complete North Ridge ascents fall Jul-Sep; Mountaineers and climber reports describe mid-July to early September with no approach snow by late July.

track.why: Logged 'Complete North Ridge' on 2024-07-27; report says the party approached from the Colchuck/Stuart Lake trailhead, climbed the Complete North Ridge, and exited at Esmeralda by car shuttle. Track reaches our summit pin within 34 m and ends 6 m from the Esmeralda pin. CAVEAT: the track's first point is ~550 m from our Stuart Lake trailhead pin (outside the 300 m rule), likely road or parking-area recording; owner may decide.

facts.text: In mid-July the glacier crossing still wants crampons and an axe, and the moat at its edge is a short drop onto a snow plug, with rock ledges just right of the gully base.
The gully above the glacier has a large chockstone about halfway; it climbs at about fourth class on good holds to the left.
